# Provenance fixtures

`C.jpg` is the signed C2PA test image of the upstream
[c2pa-rs](https://github.com/contentauth/c2pa-rs) repository
(`sdk/tests/fixtures/C.jpg`, Adobe, MIT OR Apache-2.0), vendored unchanged. It carries a real
signed manifest (issuer "C2PA Test Signing Cert", action `c2pa.created`), so the reader tests
exercise a real signature and a real hard binding. Flipping one byte of it is the negative
control.

Every other image and audio fixture is built in code (`../helpers/mediaFixtures.js`), so no
binary and no licence is committed with it.

No sample generated by Gemini or gpt-image is committed: CI has no network and no API keys. The
tests therefore prove that whatever C2PA a provider sends is preserved, not what a provider
really sends. To check that once by hand, generate an image in an iHub chat with a Gemini image
model, download it, and run it through `POST /api/eu-ai-act/provenance/_verify` (the `c2pa` member of the
answer shows whether the provider embedded a manifest).
